original_question: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N with h(N) = 0 but continuum many sequential commutation orbits, and whether there exists a II1 factor N with h(N) = 0 that is not generated as a von Neumann algebra by a single sequential commutation orbit.
target_in_paper: Problem 25 in the "Sequential commutation" section of arXiv:2511.20377: the two-part open problem asking whether there exists a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 but continuum many sequential commutation orbits, and whether there exists a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 that is not generated, as a von Neumann algebra, by a single sequential commutation orbit.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct target almost verbatim: it is the two-part open problem recorded as Problem 25, and it correctly keeps the scope on II_1 factors, the boundary case h(N)=0, continuum many sequential commutation orbits, and failure of generation by one sequential commutation orbit.
missing_details: You do not define h(N); in this context it is Hayes' 1-bounded entropy.
You do not define the ambient set on which the orbits live: the sequential commutation relation is defined on the Haar unitaries H(N), not on all elements of N.
You do not define a Haar unitary: u in U(N) with tau(u^m)=0 for all nonzero integers m.

You do not define the sequential commutation relation ~_N: for Haar unitaries u,v in N, one asks for a finite chain of Haar unitaries in an ultrapower N^U whose consecutive terms commute, beginning at u and ending at v.
You do not specify that "continuum many sequential commutation orbits" means continuum many equivalence classes of ~_N on H(N).
You do not spell out what "generated as a von Neumann algebra by a single sequential commutation orbit" means: there exists u in H(N) such that W*(O_N(u))=N, where O_N(u)={v in H(N): v~_N u}.
The draft does not make explicit that the question is about von Neumann algebra generation, not C*-generation or algebraic generation.
The draft is not fully stand-alone because it omits the ultrapower/commutator formulation that fixes the paper's intended meaning of "sequential commutation orbit."
refined_question: Let N be a II_1 factor, let h(N) denote its 1-bounded entropy, let H(N) be the set of Haar unitaries in N, and let ~_N be the sequential commutation equivalence relation on H(N), defined by u~_N v if there exist a free ultrafilter U and Haar unitaries w_1,...,w_n in N^U such that [u,w_1]=[w_k,w_{k+1}]=[w_n,v]=0 for all 1<=k<n. Writing O_N(u)={v in H(N): v~_N u}, does there exist a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 such that ~_N has continuum many equivalence classes on H(N)? And does there exist a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 such that W*(O_N(u)) is a proper subalgebra of N for every u in H(N)?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 25 itself, not a broader neighboring question. The surrounding paragraph in arXiv:2511.20377 shows that the relevant notion is the sequential commutation equivalence relation on Haar unitaries. Definition 3.1 of the cited sequential commutation paper gives the exact meaning of ~_N and of an orbit O_N(u). Lemma 5.1 there explains why the boundary case h(N)=0 is the sharp one to ask about: the von Neumann algebra generated by a single orbit has 1-bounded entropy <=0. The second clause is also naturally tied to the single-generation discussion in Internal sequential commutation and single generation, whose main theorem shows that being generated by one sequential-commutation class has strong generation consequences. So the paper-faithful refinement is to keep the two-part Problem 25 exactly as stated, while making the definitions of h(N), ~_N, H(N), O_N(u), and W*(O_N(u)) explicit.
